item.title: Typolügenchronik: The Curious History of German Typography and Other Convenient Lies
item.description: Until 1945, Germany followed Schriftkontinuität, an administrative tradition that did away with spaces between words for efficiency. It took an Allied directive for Germans to finally adopt the space — and even then, many resisted.
